name: How do you tell if a wall separating the kitchen and living room is load-bearing?

mainEntity.name: How do you tell if a wall separating the kitchen and living room is load-bearing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Determining if a kitchen wall is load-bearing requires inspecting the framing orientation in your attic, crawlspace, or basement relative to the wall. Load-bearing walls typically run perpendicular to the ceiling joists or floor joists above and often align directly over supporting beams or foundation posts below. Non-load-bearing partition walls generally run parallel to joists. Removing a load-bearing wall to create an open-concept kitchen requires installing a temporary support wall and a properly sized structural beam, which involves engineering calculations and structural plan approval during permitting.
acceptedAnswer.description: A wall is likely load-bearing if it runs perpendicular to the ceiling joists above or sits directly over basement support posts and beams.
